hints: Focus on what a termination step really is, the joining together of any two free radicals present in the mixture.
List the two different propyl radicals that can form from propane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\bullet$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}\bullet\text{CH}_3$.
Join these radicals in all A+A, A+B and B+B pairs and check which carbon skeletons match molecules 1, 2 and 3.
walkthrough:
**Recall what termination means**

Think side by side with me. Initiation makes radicals, propagation keeps them going, termination removes them by joining two radicals together to make a stable molecule.

In methane bromination:
$$2\text{CH}_3\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$$

**Identify the radicals from propane**

Propane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Removing one H gives two possible alkyl radicals.

Primary radical (n-propyl):
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\bullet$$
Secondary radical (isopropyl):
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}\bullet\text{CH}_3$$

**Combine radicals to make C6 products**

Now join every pair, bonding through the carbon with the dot.

n-propyl + isopropyl:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\bullet + \bullet\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$$
This is molecule 3, 2-methylpentane.

isopropyl + isopropyl:
$$2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}\bullet\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$$
This is molecule 2, 2,3-dimethylbutane.

**Check molecule 1 and conclude**

Molecule 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, 3-methylpentane. This needs a branched C4 fragment which cannot come from only C3 propyl radicals.

So only 2 and 3 can be formed in termination.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. Molecules 2 and 3 are correct as B+B and A+B combinations, but 1 requires a 3-methylpentane skeleton that cannot be built from two C3 propyl radicals.
options.B: Incorrect. This suggests 1 and 2 only. Molecule 2 is correct from two secondary radicals, but molecule 1 is impossible here, while molecule 3 is missed even though it is the straightforward n-propyl plus isopropyl product.
options.C: Correct. Molecule 3 is n-propyl + isopropyl giving 2-methylpentane, and molecule 2 is isopropyl + isopropyl giving 2,3-dimethylbutane. Molecule 1, 3-methylpentane, cannot be made from two propane-derived radicals.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only 1 is possible. Molecule 1 is actually the one that is impossible, as it would need ethyl or butyl radicals which are not propagation radicals in propane bromination.
